subject: Audit handoff specification and sample request — Acme Inc
messages:
From: John Tan <jtan@acme.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: audit trail handoff details needed

Hi Priya,

As part of Acme's security and procurement review for the RFP, we need a detailed specification for how Redwood will deliver audit trails and related logs if we contract for your hosted API. Specifically, please provide:

- Expected export formats (NDJSON/CSV/Parquet) and an example schema for events.
- Per-event fields you include (timestamps, request_id, event_type, model_variant, token counts, etc.).
- Ordering guarantees and how you represent partial/streamed requests.
- Checksums, manifests, and integrity proofs you provide (SHA256, signed manifests, PKI).
- Default retention windows and options for extended retention (7+ years) and legal hold handling.
- Delivery methods supported (S3 presigned, SFTP, physical media) and typical SLA for delivery.
- Any PII redaction defaults and whether you can deliver raw vs redacted payloads for an audit.
- A sample extract of ~10k events for schema validation (sanitized).

Can you send a spec and confirm whether you can provide a signed manifest with SHA256 checksums and a validation harness or acceptance script we can run? Also indicate any lead time or size estimates (GBs) for a full 90-day extraction for an average account with 1M requests/day.

Thanks,
John
John Tan
Security Program Manager, Acme Inc
security-ops@acme.com

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: John Tan <jtan@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-12T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: audit trail handoff details needed

Hi John,

Thanks for the clear list — happy to provide a complete handoff spec. I've attached the initial audit_extract_spec_v1.pdf which covers schema, delivery options, and acceptance criteria. High level answers below; the PDF has the full table and examples.

- Format and schema: primary delivery format is NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON). Each event includes: event_id, timestamp_iso8601 (UTC), request_id, user_id (hashed for hosted by default), event_type (request/response/cache_eviction), model_variant, token_count, prompt_prefix_hash (SHA256 of first N tokens), kv_cache_ops (append/read), latency_ms, and optional metadata map. We provide a JSON Schema in the attachment.

- Ordering & monotonicity: ordering is guaranteed per request_id (all tokens/segments for a request are grouped and labeled with sequence_index). Timestamps are wall-clock UTC; because of distributed clients there may be <= 5s skew. We include both event sequence_index and timestamp for reconciliation.

- Integrity & manifests: we provide a manifest.txt with SHA256 checksums for each archive (gzipped NDJSON shard). For Dedicated/Private customers we can additionally sign the manifest with an HSM-backed key on request. The manifest filename format: manifest_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_sha256.txt.

- Delivery & SLA: supported delivery methods: S3 presigned URL, customer SFTP, or encrypted transfer to a customer-managed bucket (AWS, GCP, Azure). Standard SLA for a 90-day export is 7 business days; expedited 2 business days is available for emergency e-discovery.

- Retention & legal hold: hosted default retention is 90 days. For retention beyond that (e.g. 7 years) we offer additional retention/archival add-ons or Private deployment options. Legal hold: we can freeze and export immutable snapshots; export will include an immutable manifest and chain-of-custody CSV.

- PII & redaction: by default hosted accounts receive hashed identifiers (SHA256) for user_id/prompt_prefix; raw PII redaction is governed by your DPA. For audits we can provide sanitized samples (token prefixes masked) or hashed+pepper options. Private deployments can deliver raw logs if requested under contract.

- Sample & sizing: we can produce a sanitized sample of ~10k events within 3 business days (see attachment name acme_sample_10k_events.ndjson.gz). For sizing estimates: 1M requests/day (average event ~1.2 KB compressed) -> ~36 GB per month compressed; final number depends on token counts and metadata.

- Acceptance & validation: included acceptance criteria: schema validation, manifest checksums, record counts, and a validation script (validate_extract.sh) we host in the Drive link. We'll provide checksums and a short validation harness so you can run the same checks on delivery.

Next steps: I will upload the sample (sanitized) and the manifest, and share a Drive link for the spec and scripts. Please confirm preferred delivery method (S3 presigned or SFTP) and whether you need raw user identifiers for the sample.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0123

Attachment: audit_extract_spec_v1.pdf
From: John Tan <jtan@acme.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: security-ops@acme.com
Date: 2026-06-14T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit handoff specification and sample request

Priya,

This is helpful — a few follow-ups from our compliance team before we accept the sample: 

1) Sample rate & representativeness: please confirm the sampling method for the 10k sample (random across time, stratified by model_variant, or last-N). We want to ensure the sample covers production spikes.

2) Redaction & re-identification risk: if user_id is hashed, is there a salt/pepper applied unique per-customer? Can you provide details on how prompt_prefix_hash is generated and whether it can be reversed under any circumstance?

3) Partial exports / incremental: if we request an ongoing daily incremental export, can you guarantee non-overlap and continuing sequence indices?

4) Chain-of-custody & signed manifests: for legal hold do you support manifest signing (cert) and a timeline that demonstrates who initiated the export? We need logs of the export job with operator identity.

5) Encryption & key management: can you encrypt delivered archives with a customer-managed key (CMK)? For Private deployments we expect full KMS/HSM integration.

Also, please send the sample to security-ops@acme.com; if possible, include the SHA256 manifest file so our team can run the validation harness.

Thanks,
John

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: John Tan <jtan@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-15T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Audit handoff specification and sample request

Hi John,

Short answers:
- Sampling: sample is stratified by model_variant and by day-of-week with random selection within strata to capture spikes; we'll note the sampling seed in metadata.
- Hashing: hosted accounts use a per-customer salt stored in the key vault; prompt_prefix_hash is SHA256(prefix_bytes + salt). We do not store raw prompt prefixes for hosted customers. Private customers can request raw identifiers under contract.
- Incremental exports: we provide incremental shards with non-overlapping sequence windows and a manifest that includes start_index and end_index for each shard; consumers can detect and reconcile gaps by comparing manifests.
- Chain-of-custody: manifests include operator_id, job_id, and UTC timestamps. For Dedicated/Private customers we can sign manifests with an HSM key and provide an audit trail of the export job (who initiated, job logs).
- Encryption/CMK: yes — for S3 delivery we can encrypt with a customer-managed KMS key (AWS KMS CMK) or provide an encrypted archive wrapped with a customer public key.

We will:
- Upload acme_sample_10k_events.ndjson.gz (sanitized) and sha256_manifest.txt to a presigned S3 location and email security-ops@acme.com today.
- Include the validation script and the spec PDF in the Drive folder.

If you want the HSM-signed manifest for this sample, let us know and we'll sign it; for contract-level exports we recommend configuring the HSM signing during onboarding.

Regards,
Priya

Attachment: acme_sample_10k_events.ndjson.gz, sha256_manifest.txt
